comments.quote_zh: 这可能是关于这个大致主题有史以来最好的一场演讲
comments.text_zh: 这可能是关于这个大致主题有史以来最好的一场演讲：[VIDEO] [Growing a language by Guy Steele]，说真的，有时间一定看看，也请务必忍受一下开头看起来很奇怪。但快到结尾时它问了这个问题（大意是）：一种语言应该原生实现复数吗？应该原生实现 numbers module n 吗？区间数或有理数呢？我也讨厌对晦涩符号的荒唐重载，但两个极端都不好。不允许重载会让你写成 BigDecimal.of(3).add(BigDecimal.ONE).divide…，而毫无限制地允许重载，会让你搞出 msg #!! something 之类的东西。但也许一个合理的折中是只允许基本运算符（+、-、*、/）可重载。
comments.text: This is probably the best talk ever on the general topic: [VIDEO] [Growing a language by Guy Steele], seriously give it a look if you have the time and do put up with the seemingly strange start. But at around the end it asks this (paraphrasing): Should a language have complex numbers implemented natively? Should it have numbers module n implemented natively? What about intervals, or rational numbers? I also dislike the ridiculous overloading of cryptic symbols, but neither extreme is good. Not allowing overloading will give you BigDecimal.of(3).add(BigDecimal.ONE).divide… , while allowing it unrestricted will give you things like msg #!! something. But perhaps a sane middle ground is to allow only basic operators (+,-,*,/) to be overloadable.

comments.story_title: For Better or for Worse
comments.why_zh: Steele 对 Worse is Better 和语言生长的看法
comments.quote_zh: 尽管年头已久，仍值得一看
comments.text_zh: 我最近看了 Guy Steele 的“Growing a Language”演讲。它和 jmoiron 在这里的帖子非常相关，而且尽管年头已久，仍值得一看：[VIDEO] 在我看来，Steele 对“Worse is Better”的评论，比这里关于 Go 所表达的那套说法，更好地代表了那篇原始文章。Steele 说：“‘Worse is Better’的要旨是：要让一种语言被许多人使用，最好的办法不是去设计和构建‘The Right Thing’，因为那会花太久。在一场竞赛中，一门有瑕疵的小语言会击败一门设计良好的语言，因为用户不会等待那个正确的东西；他们会使用快速而便宜的语言，并忍受那些瑕疵。一旦一门小语言占据了一个生态位，就很难取代它的位置。”换句话说，‘Worse is Better’的教训是：把一个‘足够好’的东西推向市场，并受益于其广泛使用带来的网络效应，总会击败把‘真正好’的东西推向同一类别市场，因为延迟的代价就是（社区）网络效应的损失。这里说明性的例子是 UNIX 和 C，但它很容易被交叉应用到更近期的项目上。从这个角度看，Go 并不是‘Worse is Better’的好例子。它占据着和 C 相同的生态位，却晚了近 40 年才出现。它似乎是一门“C 的第二版”，设计时带着非常明确的目标：纠正 C 作为系统编程语言的特定缺陷，但不带有那种……范围蔓延
comments.text: I recently watched Guy Steele's "Growing a Language" talk. It's very much related to jmoiron's post here, and is worth a watch despite its age: [VIDEO] Steele's commentary on "Worse is Better" seems to me to be a better representation of the original essay than the one expressed here about Go. Steele says: "The gist of ['Worse is Better'] is that the best way to get a language used by many persons is not to design and build 'The Right Thing,' because that will take too long. In a race, a small language with warts will beat a well designed language because users will not wait for the right thing; they will use the language that is quick and cheap, and put up with the warts. Once a small language fills a niche, it is hard to take its place." In other words, the lesson of 'Worse is Better' is that getting a 'good enough' thing to market, and benefiting from the network effects of its widespread use, will always beat getting the 'the really good' thing to market in the same category, because the cost of delay is the loss of (community) network effects. The illustrative example here is UNIX and C, but it can be easily cross-applied to more recent projects. From that vantage point, Go isn't a good example of 'Worse is Better'. It occupies the same niche as C, but was delivered nearly 4 decades later. comments.quote_zh: Steele 的 Growing A Language[0] 演讲特别指出，封装是程序的核心构建块。
comments.text_zh: 你论证的逻辑极端，就是把所有东西都做成带 class 的 `div`。虽然这并非不可能，但这种模型的主要问题在于，它没有提供任何封装策略。封装是程序员构建复杂程序的核心工具之一，所以在模板语言中为它提供一等支持，会突然让很多事情变得容易得多。没有封装，很多事情会变得更令人沮丧。事件冒泡必须被微观管理。开发者工具也没那么有用。处理相互冲突的 CSS ID 会变得更加令人沮丧。Steele 的 Growing A Language[0] 演讲特别指出，封装是程序的核心构建块。考虑到如今 HTML 的使用方式（React + Angular 都是“HTML 作为程序布局”的模型），缺少封装就是一种拐杖 [0]：[VIDEO]
comments.text: The logical extreme of your argument is to make everything a `div` with classes. While possible, the main issue with that model is that it provides no encapsulation strategy. Encapsulation is one of the core tools for programmers for building complex programs, so having first class support for that in the templating language suddenly makes a lot of things easier. Without encapsulation, a lot of things become more frustrating. Event bubbling has to be micro-managed. Dev tools are less useful. It becomes even more frustrating to deal with conflicting CSS IDs. Steele's Growing A Language[0] talk specifically points to encapsulation as the core building blog for programs. Given how HTML is used nowadays (React + Angular are both "HTML as program layouts" models), not having encapsulation is a crutch [0]: [VIDEO]

comments.text: > Of course, I also accept that maybe the current vernacular is degrading.
